claims.text: Users tend to overestimate the accuracy of LLM responses when provided with default explanations.
Longer LLM explanations increase user confidence even when the extra length does not improve answer accuracy.
Adjusting LLM explanations to better reflect internal confidence narrows the calibration gap between human confidence and model confidence.
Adjusting LLM explanations to better reflect internal confidence narrows the discrimination gap in distinguishing correct from incorrect answers.
Adjusting LLM explanations to better reflect internal confidence improves user perception of LLM accuracy.

evidence.description: Experiments with multiple-choice and short-answer questions reveal that users tend to overestimate accuracy when provided default explanations.
User confidence increased with longer explanations even when extra length provided no improvement in answer accuracy.
Adjusting explanations to reflect internal model confidence resulted in a narrowed calibration gap.
Adjusting explanations to reflect internal model confidence resulted in a narrowed discrimination gap.
Adjusting explanations to reflect internal model confidence significantly improved user perception of LLM accuracy.

methodologies.name: Human evaluation of LLM response confidence and accuracy
methodologies.description: Behavioral experiments evaluating user confidence, calibration gap, and discrimination gap using multiple-choice and short-answer questions under default and confidence-adjusted LLM explanation conditions.

limitations.text: Less is understood about how effectively LLMs convey uncertainty to users compared to their internal confidence assessment.
